hook: Two bus routes get a commuter to work. Route 2 is usually a little faster, but now and then it takes 45 minutes or more. Route 1 is slower on a typical day but very steady. Which is better depends on what you need, and to decide, you have to compare whole distributions: shape, center, spread and outliers, not just one number.

prereq.q: Which summary is the length of the box in a boxplot?
What does a standard deviation of 4 points tell you about test scores?
options: Scores typically differ from the mean by about 4 points
The highest score is 4 above the median
prereq.why: The standard deviation is a typical distance from the mean.

figure.caption: Top: parallel boxplots compare two groups on one scale. Bottom: a z-score measures distance from the mean in standard deviations.

chain.cause: Two groups are measured on the same variable
chain.effect: graph them on one scale, such as parallel boxplots or stacked dotplots

chain.cause: Compare shape, center, spread and unusual features
chain.effect: use comparing words (greater, less variable) with numbers for each feature, in context

chain.cause: Two values come from different distributions
chain.effect: compare their positions, not their raw sizes

chain.cause: Subtract the mean and divide by the standard deviation
chain.effect: the z-score puts both on one scale: standard deviations above or below their own mean

ideas: Compare distributions on every feature: shape, center, spread and outliers, each with a comparing word and numbers, in context.
A z-score is $z = \frac{x - \bar{x}}{s}$ (or $\frac{x - \mu}{\sigma}$ for a population): how many standard deviations a value is above (+) or below (−) the mean. It has no units.
Relative position compares values from different groups: z-scores and percentiles do this; raw values do not.
The median of combined groups is not the average of their medians.

misconception.wrong: Route 1’s median is 31 minutes and Route 2’s median is 28 minutes. (Given as a comparison.)
misconception.right: That lists numbers but compares nothing. Say "Route 1 has a greater median travel time (31 minutes) than Route 2 (28 minutes)."

summary: To compare distributions, describe each feature (shape, center, spread, outliers) with a comparing word and numbers, in context. To compare single values from different distributions, use relative position: the z-score $z = \frac{x - \bar{x}}{s}$ counts standard deviations from the mean, and a percentile gives the percent of values at or below.
